note: What this domain can compute, written for a reader rather than for a caller. A catalog entry describes one capability, and most of what is here is not a capability of its own: it is a method that submitted code imports as `primitives.<module>`. Nothing lists those, so nothing could show them, and a person reading what the product does saw two entries where there are twenty one methods. Every module below is a real file in `kernels/primitives/`, and a check fails if that stops being true in either direction.

methods.name: Hypothesis Tests
methods.what: Paired, unpaired and unequal variance t-tests, one way and two way ANOVA, and a per feature test for volcano summaries.

methods.name: Correlation
methods.what: Correlates any two sets of features, every pair at once. Corrected within subject where the data is repeated measures, with the uncorrected estimate reported beside it.

methods.name: Regression
methods.what: Linear, polynomial, multiple, logistic and regularized models, with effect sizes and confidence intervals.

methods.name: Mixed Models
methods.what: Random intercept models for repeated measures, fitted to one feature or to many in one call.

methods.name: Survival
methods.what: Kaplan-Meier curves by group and Cox models. You define the event and the censoring.

methods.name: Prediction
methods.what: Decision trees, random forests and gradient boosting, with a cross validated score and feature importances.

methods.name: Partial Least Squares
methods.what: Projects many collinear features onto a few components that track the outcome, and ranks features by importance.

methods.name: Ordination
methods.what: Principal coordinates from a distance matrix, with tests for whether groups separate and whether their spread differs.

methods.name: Distances
methods.what: Distance between every pair of samples, by Bray-Curtis, Jaccard, Canberra, Euclidean and others.

methods.name: Diversity
methods.what: Within sample diversity, with every index named for exactly what it computes.

methods.name: Dimensionality Reduction
methods.what: Projects many features onto a few axes with t-SNE, for looking at structure.

methods.name: Clustering
methods.what: Groups samples by density, and reports how well separated the groups are.

methods.name: Association Rules
methods.what: Finds features that occur together more often than chance, with support, confidence and lift.

methods.name: Mediation
methods.what: Splits the effect of one variable on another into a direct path and a path through a mediator, with a bootstrapped interval.

methods.name: Confounding
methods.what: Variance inflation for collinear predictors, and change in estimate testing for candidate confounders.

methods.name: Multiple Testing
methods.what: False discovery rate control across a set of tests, by Benjamini-Hochberg, Bonferroni or Holm.

methods.name: Repeated Measurements
methods.what: Collapses a subject's repeated measurements into one value per feature, by mean, median, first, last, slope or area under the curve.

methods.name: Transformations
methods.what: Centered log ratio, log, total sum scaling and Fisher z, and filtering features by how often and how strongly they appear.

methods.name: Feature Ratios
methods.what: Ratios and log ratios of one feature to another, across every sample at once.

methods.name: Descriptive Summaries
methods.what: Mean, median, variance, standard deviation, range, sum, minimum and maximum.

methods.name: Histograms
methods.what: Bins a distribution, with the bin width chosen by a stated rule or set by hand.
